messages.author: Juliette Newell
messages.body:
Dear Sir/Madam,
I am currently using the amber MD software to run simulations looking at peptide self-assembly.
I am trying to run a simulation in a vacuum, however when I get to the equilibration step I get the error:
'Error: ifbox=2 in prmtop but angles are not correct'
My tleap script is:
source leaprc.gaff2
source leaprc.protein.ff14SB
source keaprc.water.tip3p
CDPA = loadmol2 CDPA.mol2
loadamberparams CDPA2.frcmod
saveoff CDPA2.lib
loadoff CDPA2.lib
solvateoct CDPA CDPA 25
check CDPA
saveamberparm CDPA CDPA2.top CDPA2.crd
Are you able to suggest why I may be getting the error?
Best wishes,
Juliette

messages.author: Carlos Simmerling
messages.body:
your leap script adds water (solvateoct), so this isn't set up for
vacuum simulations.

messages.author: Carlos Simmerling
messages.body:
Hi Juliette,
If you want a true vacuum simulation, then don't add water and just build
it without the solvate command. The vacuum environment is quite different
from solution, though, so you might want to think about whether this is a
good match for what you want to learn about self-assembly (unless you truly
want to study it in vacuum, like in the gas phase).
carlos

messages.author: Carlos Simmerling
messages.body:
I'm not sure exactly what you're doing in the script, but it looks like
you're solvating CDPA with other copies of CDPA. if that's your goal, it
might work,  though the *packmol program *might be a more useful option. if
you want to try using the one build by leap, then it would be helpful to
see the full output from the MD run that gave the error.
